reason: FindObjectOfType is significantly slower and has undefined ordering. FindAnyObjectByType is faster when you do not need a deterministic result. FindFirstObjectByType uses instance ID ordering.
New API requires an explicit sort mode, allowing the engine to skip sorting when not needed, which is substantially faster for large scenes.
Same performance improvements as the generic version. The non-generic overloads are also deprecated in favor of type-safe generics.

replacement: HLSLPROGRAM / ENDHLSL with URP or HDRP shader libraries
reason: CG shaders use the legacy built-in pipeline surface shader compiler. HLSL is required for SRP (URP/HDRP) and gives access to modern shader features.
Resources folder increases build size, cannot be updated without a full rebuild, and all assets in it are included in the build whether referenced or not.

replacement: InputSystem via InputAction, PlayerInput component, or generated C# input class
reason: The legacy Input Manager lacks action remapping, composite bindings, per-device input, and proper gamepad support. The new Input System is required for modern platforms.

replacement: Direct method calls, C# events, UnityEvent, or ScriptableObject event channels
reason: SendMessage uses string-based reflection, is slow, not type-safe, and causes silent failures if the method name is misspelled. Direct references or event patterns are safer and faster.

replacement: Cache Camera.main in a field during Awake/Start
reason: Camera.main performs FindGameObjectWithTag internally each call. In Unity 2020+, it is cached per frame, but caching it yourself is still clearer and avoids null-check overhead.

replacement: Cache references in Awake/Start, use serialized fields, or dependency injection
reason: GameObject.Find traverses the entire hierarchy by name each call. It is O(n) per invocation and should never run per-frame.
Coroutines cannot return values, have awkward error handling, allocate on yield, and cannot be composed. Awaitable supports structured async with proper cancellation and exception propagation.
Mono is being phased out. IL2CPP provides better performance, smaller builds on most platforms, and is the only backend available on consoles, iOS, and WebGL.

replacement: Netcode for GameObjects (NGO) or third-party (Mirror, FishNet, Photon Fusion)
reason: UNet was deprecated and removed. Netcode for GameObjects is Unity's official replacement with server-authoritative architecture and modern transport layer.
PUN2 is in maintenance mode. Fusion provides tick-based simulation, state authority, and better scalability. Quantum offers a deterministic ECS approach for competitive games.
Manually writing UXMLFactory boilerplate is no longer needed. The UxmlElement and UxmlAttribute attributes auto-generate the factory and traits classes.

legacy: OnGUI / GUILayout / EditorGUILayout for editor tools
replacement: UI Toolkit (VisualElement, UXML, USS) for editor UI
reason: IMGUI redraws every frame and does not support styling or layout persistence. UI Toolkit provides retained-mode UI with CSS-like styling, data binding, and better performance.
AssetDatabase is editor-only and will cause build failures if used in runtime code. Use Addressables or serialized references for runtime asset loading.

replacement: JSON serialization to Application.persistentDataPath or a save system
reason: PlayerPrefs is stored in the registry on Windows and has size limits. It is not encrypted, not portable, and not suitable for structured save data.
